question: According to data from the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), almost 200 000 hectares burned in Galicia in the summer of 2025, making the autonomous community one of the most heavily affected regions in Europe.

The Galician Government’s failure to take preventive action resulted in a lack of response to this tragedy, with the fires laying waste to many productive areas and homes, as well as a lot of infrastructure, particularly in the province of Ourense.

Moreover, as the Galician delegation informed the Commission’s Director-General for the Environment at a meeting a few weeks ago, the restoration plans have not been fulfilled, with only 6 000 hectares having been restored. In view of the above: 1.
Will the Commission urge the Galician Government to restore the areas affected by the fires?
What EU funds has the Galician Government used to restore the areas that burned in 2025?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.10.2026) The Commission has closely monitored the impact of the 2025 wildfires in Galicia. Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plans 2023–20271, support is available for sustainable forest management, fire prevention and forest restoration.

In Galicia, EUR 833 million in total public expenditure has been programmed, including EUR 76 million for forest damage prevention and EUR 8 million for forest restoration. So far, EUR 12 million and EUR 309 000 respectively have been executed.

Under the previous Galician Rural Development Programme, measures for forest-fire and natural-disaster prevention, and for restoring damaged production potential, were also programmed. Between 2016-2025, around EUR 240 million was spent on prevention and EUR 16 million on restoration. In 2025, annual allocations were about EUR 11 million and EUR 2 million respectively.

Interventions funded by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development and European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) are under shared management: Spanish authorities are responsible for selecting operations, allocating budgets and delivering support in line with EU rules, while the Commission monitors the proper use of EU funds without replacing the competent regional authorities.

Under Galicia’s 2021–2027 ERDF programme, EUR 27.5 million (priority P2E RESTORE) has been earmarked for investments responding to the summer 2025 forest fires, based on the ‘build back better’ principle and covering prevention, recovery, rehabilitation and postdisaster reconstruction. Selected operations exceed EUR 9 million, with a further EUR 9.5 million in the pipeline. Moreover, Spain received EUR 120.
5 million from the EU Solidarity Fund for essential emergency operations, including in Galicia.
